finding.claim: dropTable ignores the error returned by Authorize(u, "dba"), so any authenticated user can reach DROP TABLE.
finding.source: Any authenticated request to /admin/drop; the user is taken from the request context (api.go:25).

trace.note: /admin/drop is registered to dropTable with no middleware in this file
userFrom(r) reads the user from request context
Authorize(u, "dba") error is discarded; no return on failure
DDL executes regardless of authorization result

finding.guards_checked: Authorize is called but its result is ignored, so it is not a control. No if-err-return, no route-level middleware in this file, no HTTP method restriction. vacuum (api.go:33-35) checks the error correctly, which confirms this is an omission. Caveat: the middleware that sets the "user" context key is not in this directory; if absent, the assertion at api.go:22 panics instead of executing.

verdict.guard_found: none effective. Authorize(u, "dba") at api.go:26 is a bare statement, so its error return is discarded and execution continues to runSQL at api.go:27. The only route registration is api.go:44 with no middleware. vacuum at api.go:33-35 checks the error correctly, which shows the omission.
verdict.reason: Any user whose context carries a "user" value can reach runSQL("DROP TABLE " + ...) at api.go:27 because Authorize's error at api.go:26 is ignored and /admin/drop (api.go:44) has no middleware. The caveat is that the middleware that sets the "user" context key is outside this directory, so whether it enforces a role cannot be checked here; if it fails open, the flaw is reachable by an anonymous caller.

finding.claim: The table name t from r.FormValue("t") is concatenated into a DROP TABLE statement, allowing SQL/DDL injection.
finding.source: r.FormValue("t") at api.go:27: query string or form body, attacker-controlled by any HTTP client.
finding.sink: runSQL at api.go:27, receiving the concatenated DDL string

trace.note: r.FormValue("t") read and concatenated into "DROP TABLE " + t
Result passed to runSQL as a raw string

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist of table names, no identifier quoting, no parameter binding, no validation of t. Reachable by any authenticated user via F1. Even a legitimate DBA is exposed to stacked or break-out payloads in t. Caveat: runSQL is an empty stub in this file, so stacked-query behavior is inferred from the string built, not observed.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize(u, "dba") at api.go:26 is the only control. It returns an error that is discarded as a bare statement, so it blocks nothing. No table-name allowlist, identifier quoting, parameter binding, or validation exists at api.go:27. The vacuum handler at api.go:33-35 checks the error correctly, which shows the missing check in dropTable is a bug and not a design choice.
verdict.reason: api.go:27 concatenates the raw form value r.FormValue("t") into "DROP TABLE " + t and passes it to runSQL, and the only authorization check at api.go:26 discards its error, so any caller with a user in context (set by middleware not present in this file) reaches the DDL. The trace is accurate; the claim that runSQL executes stacked statements is inferred because runSQL is an empty stub at api.go:41, and the reachability through F1 is not verifiable from this file alone.
